The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup
podcast.body: After the departure of Noah Weiland and the arrangement with a new singer proved unsuccessful, Suspect 208 eventually broke up. "A new singer was found, but that arrangement did not last. And Suspect 208 broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation After Suspect 208
podcast.body: St. Electric is a new band formed by London Hudson and Nico St. Geras, along with three other members, following the dissolution of Suspect 208. "However, London Hudson and Nico St. Geras have a new band, at last word anyway, called St. Electric with three other people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Comparison
podcast.body: The band's sound is described as "very STP-ish," drawing a comparison to Stone Temple Pilots. "Very STP is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Non-Famous Parentage
podcast.body: Nico St. Geras was a member of Suspect 208 and later St. Electric, and is explicitly noted as not having a famous father, differentiating him from other band members. "There was a fourth member, Nico St. Geras, but I don't think he had a famous father."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Short-Lived Formation
podcast.body: Suspect 208 struggled to maintain its lineup, with vocalist Noah Weiland being dismissed shortly after the band's formation due to reported issues with attending rehearsals. "Unfortunately, Suspect 208 just could not hold it together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
